english.title: Attempted racially / religiously aggravated harassment / alarm / distress - words / writing
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with intent to cause **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) harassment, alarm or distress, attempted to

(A)_[use threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour or disorderly behaviour]_
(B)_[display some writing, sign or other visible representation which was threatening, abusive or insulting]_

and the offence was

(C)_[racially]_
(D)_[religiously]_

aggravated within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 31(1)(b) and (4) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
with intent to cause harassment/alarm/distress
attempted touse threatening/abusive/insulting words or behaviour or disorderly behaviour OR
display any writing/sign/other visible representation which was threatening/abusive/insulting
and the offence was racially/religiously aggravated

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is NOT available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) If on a trial on Indictment of a person charged with this offence the jury find him not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the basic offence contrary to section 4A of the Public Order Act 1986.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
